title: Repulsion-Driven $p - i p$ Superconductivity in a Single Valley Revealed by DMRG
authors: Cesar A. Gallegos, Omid Tavakol, Christopher Yang, Steven R. White, Thomas Scaffidi
abstract: We demonstrate repulsion-driven topological superconductivity of a single species of Dirac fermions, motivated by valley-polarized phases observed in two-dimensional materials such as rhombohedral graphene. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations on the Qi-Wu-Zhang lattice model on cylinders of width up to eight, we find a robust phase of spinless chiral $p$-wave superconductivity. Pairing already starts at low doping and thus occurs on a small, nearly isotropic Fermi pocket, and is therefore not tied to the particular details or anisotropy of the dispersion but instead seems tied to the non-trivial quantum geometry of the bands. In fact, the winding of the superconductor order parameter is opposite ("$p-ip$") to that of the anomalous Hall metal which forms the parent state, in agreement with expectations recently derived from weak coupling calculations. At larger doping, we find that a pair-density-wave component develops alongside zero-momentum pairing. Our work shows that the combination of strong repulsion, absence of time-reversal in the parent state, and non-trivial quantum geometry form a promising platform to realize topological superconductivity.
summary: This paper uses DMRG simulations on the QWZ model to show that strong repulsive interactions can induce topological p-ip superconductivity in a single valley of Dirac fermions. The SC state is robustly found upon doping and coexists with a pair-density-wave component at higher doping levels. This work highlights the crucial role of strong correlations and non-trivial band geometry in realizing exotic superconducting phases.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate the existence and nature of repulsion-driven topological superconductivity in a single valley of Dirac fermions.
main_result: The authors find robust evidence for spinless chiral p-wave superconductivity ($p-ip$) upon doping, which is driven by strong repulsive interactions and non-trivial band geometry.
method: Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations are extensively used on lattice cylinders to map out the phase diagram as a function of doping and interaction strength.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using the interacting Qi-Wu-Zhang (QWZ) lattice model, which captures physics relevant to valley-polarized 2D materials like rhombohedral graphene. The Hamiltonian includes kinetic terms and a strong on-site repulsive interaction ($U$).
key_observables: Superconducting order parameter ($\Delta$), average occupation ($n_A, n_B$), pair-density-wave (PDW) component, and the momentum distribution $n(\mathbf{k})$ across the Fermi surface.
important_parameters: Strong repulsion regime ($U$ large), hole-doping ($\mu < \mu_c$), and the specific topological nature of the parent state (anomalous Hall metal).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on DMRG on cylinders, which is suitable for identifying phase boundaries, and the focus is on the minimal case of a single Dirac fermion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QWZ model, the non-interacting band structure, and DMRG scans showing the transition from an insulator to the $p-ip$ SC phase, and subsequently to a PDW+SC phase.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the model (QWZ), applying DMRG to find the SC phase upon doping, detailing the crossover from quasi-1D to isotropic SC, and finally characterizing the coexisting PDW+SC state using momentum-space analysis.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete theoretical realization of topological superconductivity driven purely by repulsive interactions in a geometrically constrained system, offering insights applicable to strongly correlated electronic materials.
